commit.message:
fix: handle getpass.getuser() failure in workflow info header (#4322)

The `Workflow.info_header` property calls `askpass.getuser()`, which can
raise an exception in certain contexts (in my case, a Docker container
run as a non-root user, so no entry for UID in `/etc/passwd`). This
catches the potential exceptions and uses the value `"unavailable"`
(matching the case for `config_md5` above).

The documentation for `getuser()` in Python 3.13+ explicitly says it
raises `OSError`, but previous versions raised other exceptions (but
does not specify which). I could not find a good source on exactly what
the possible exceptions were on 3.11 and 3.12. In my case above it was
`KeyError`. The decision to catch `KeyError` and `ImportError` in
addition to `OSError` were based on conversations with two different AI
agents, which both gave the same recommendation.
